name: What Nobody Tells a New Business Analyst
title: What Nobody Tells a New Business Analyst
subtitle: BA training teaches you to write a user story. It doesn't teach you who's allowed to approve it, how big it really is, or what to do when two stakeholders both think they're the priority.

cover.alt: What Nobody Tells a New Business Analyst: the org chart is your real onboarding; everything looks the same size until it isn't; don't quietly pick a side; jargon is easy, the real work isn't; always ask who besides the requester has to agree
cover.caption: Better questions. Smoother delivery. A stronger BA.
cover.use: Cover: top of the post (and Substack social preview)

substack.email_subject: The job description says "gather requirements." It skips the hard parts.
substack.note:
A new BA can write a user story, draft acceptance criteria and run a meeting.

Then a stakeholder asks for something, and the work stalls on three questions no training deck covers:

Who's allowed to say yes to this?
How big is it, really?
What happens when the person two desks over wants the opposite?
